issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Nigerian qualifications attract verification, equivalency downgrades and outright scepticism - a discount applied to the document rather than the holder.

details.aspect: Verification as standard, at the applicant's cost
details.description: Transcripts and certificates are sent to third-party evaluators and to the issuing institution. The fee and the wait are the applicant's, and an unanswered verification is treated as a failure.
details.energy_note: Genuine, and checked anyway, at your expense.

details.aspect: Equivalency downgrades
details.description: A four-year Nigerian degree may be assessed as equivalent to less than a bachelor's in some systems, requiring a bridging year before postgraduate entry.
details.energy_note: Four years of study, assessed as three.

details.aspect: Professional requalification is the real cost
details.description: Doctors, nurses, engineers, lawyers and accountants re-sit examinations, complete supervised practice and pay for both while working below their level.
details.energy_note: Qualified twice, paid once.

details.aspect: HONEST GAP - the strike-gap suspicion is not documented
details.description: No sourced evidence was found that credential evaluators specifically flagged 2022-2023 Nigerian transcripts as suspicious because of the irregular date gaps created by the ASUU strike. The concern is widely expressed in Nigerian commentary and is recorded here as unverified.
details.energy_note: Plausible, widely feared, and not demonstrated.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - assessed as three years
details.description: Her four-year Nigerian bachelor's is evaluated abroad as equivalent to three years of study. The master's she was admitted to requires a full bachelor's equivalent, so she is offered a bridging year at GBP 14,000 that teaches her material she covered in her second year.
details.energy_note: A year and fourteen thousand pounds, to re-learn her second year.

issues.title: NYSC, and a year the state assigns you
issues.category_name: Education, strikes and a certificate nobody abroad trusts
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
issues.summary: The National Youth Service Corps posts graduates for a year to a state not of their choosing, and completion is required for much formal employment.

details.aspect: It is a gate, not an option
details.description: The discharge certificate is required for federal employment and many private employers, so the year is not electable.
details.energy_note: A compulsory year, before you may be hired.

details.aspect: Posting can be to an insecure state
details.description: Assignment is national, so a graduate may be posted to a state affected by the conditions in SEC-001 and SEC-003. Redeployment requests exist and are discretionary.
details.energy_note: Sent, by the state, to where the state cannot protect you.

details.aspect: For women it raises specific risks and specific costs
details.description: Accommodation, travel and safety in an unfamiliar state, plus the marriage-based redeployment route that exists for married women and not for single ones - which quietly rewards marrying before service.
details.energy_note: A redeployment route that requires a husband.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the posting letter
details.description: She is posted to a state that was in the news twice in the preceding six months. Redeployment on medical grounds requires documentation she does not have; on marital grounds requires a husband she does not have. She goes.
details.energy_note: Two exemptions, and she qualifies for neither.

issues.title: Sex for grades
issues.category_name: Harassment: the lecturer, the manager, the open secret
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
issues.summary: The transaction is well enough known to have a name, and it was documented on camera at two of the region's most prestigious universities.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the BBC Africa Eye investigation
details.description: Reporter Kiki Mordi and three other undercover reporters spent nine months on the investigation and three months filming with hidden cameras at the University of Lagos and the University of Ghana. The footage showed lecturers harassing, propositioning and attempting to blackmail the reporters in closed-door meetings.
details.energy_note: Filmed, broadcast, and the lecturers suspended.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the reporter's own case
details.description: Mordi said one of her professors withheld her exam results for two semesters because she refused his advances, which led her to drop out and give up becoming a doctor. She tried to report it at the time and says it was clear nothing would be done.
details.money_note: A medical career, not had.
details.energy_note: Two semesters withheld, and a different life.

details.aspect: The power is over the result, which is the point
details.description: The lecturer controls the mark, the resit, the project supervision and the reference. Refusal is not a single unpleasant conversation; it is a threat to the degree already paid for.
details.energy_note: He is not asking. He is holding your transcript.

details.aspect: 'Pervasive' and 'an open secret'
details.description: The executive director of a Nigerian education nonprofit described the problem as pervasive in Nigeria and like an open secret. The African Feminist Initiative tied it to unequal power relations and abuse of power predominantly by male faculty.
details.energy_note: Everyone knows. That is the state of the problem.

details.aspect: The response was suspension and a bill
details.description: Both universities suspended the lecturers filmed, one implicated lecturer's church asked him to step down, and the Nigerian Senate reintroduced legislation criminalising sexual advances by lecturers toward students with mandatory jail time. One of those filmed called the documentary a hoax.
details.energy_note: Suspensions, a bill, and a denial.

details.aspect: What the documentary changed, and did not
details.description: Many women across Nigerian universities shared similar experiences after broadcast. The structural condition - one man controlling one woman's degree outcome with no independent marking - was not altered by any of it.
details.energy_note: A national conversation, and the same marking system.

issues.title: The workplace version
issues.category_name: Harassment: the lecturer, the manager, the open secret
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
issues.summary: The same structure moves into employment: a man with discretion over hiring, confirmation, promotion or payment, and no functioning complaint route.

details.aspect: Complaint routes that report to the problem
details.description: In small and medium firms the HR function, where it exists, reports to the person complained about. In the informal sector, which is 93% of employment, there is no function at all.
details.energy_note: Complaining to the man who appointed him.

details.aspect: The cost of refusing is the job
details.description: Loss of a contract, a shift, a confirmation or a reference in a labour market where replacement is easy and recourse is nil.
details.energy_note: Refusing, and being replaced by Monday.

details.aspect: It shapes which sectors women will enter
details.description: Fields with reputations for this lose female applicants, which reproduces the male dominance that produced the reputation.
details.energy_note: Avoiding an industry, and thereby confirming its composition.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the confirmation meeting
details.description: Her six-month probation ends on the 30th. On the 22nd her line manager suggests dinner to 'discuss her development'. She declines, citing her mother's health. On the 30th her probation is extended by three months for reasons described as performance-related.
details.energy_note: Extended probation, performance-related, on paper.

issues.title: Being harassed and being the one who is judged
issues.category_name: Harassment: the lecturer, the manager, the open secret
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
issues.summary: Disclosure carries a reputational cost to the woman, which is why prevalence is understated everywhere including in this dataset.

details.aspect: The question is what she did
details.description: What she wore, why she was there, why she went to his office, why she did not report it immediately. The inquiry reorients onto the complainant automatically.
details.energy_note: An investigation that turns around to face her.

details.aspect: Which makes non-disclosure rational
details.description: If reporting costs the degree, the job and the reputation and produces no sanction, silence is the correct strategy - and every dataset built on reports therefore undercounts.
details.energy_note: A number nobody has, for reasons that are themselves the harm.

details.aspect: And the low numbers are then used as evidence
details.description: Few formal complaints is read as few incidents, which is used to argue against the legislation that would make complaining survivable.
details.energy_note: Silence, counted as absence, and cited as proof.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the group chat
details.description: She tells two colleagues. Within a week it is known, and the version circulating has her at fault in a way the original did not. She stops mentioning it, which is recorded by everyone as the matter being resolved.
details.energy_note: Telling two people, and watching it change shape.

issues.title: The statistics that say there is no problem
issues.category_name: Work, unemployment and what a degree is worth
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
issues.summary: Nigeria's headline unemployment rate is around 4%, which is lower than Germany's. The number is not wrong; it is measuring something other than what people mean by unemployment.

details.aspect: The methodology change, and the two series
details.description: Under the old methodology unemployment rose from 14.2% in 2016 to 33.3% in 2020. Under the new ILO-aligned methodology, Q2 2024 unemployment was 4.3% with time-related underemployment at 9.2%. The two series are not comparable.
details.energy_note: Thirty-three per cent, then four, and nothing changed on the ground.

details.aspect: What the low number conceals
details.description: Self-employment was 85.6% of employment in Q2 2024 and informal employment was 93.0%. An hour of petty trading in a week counts as employed, which is methodologically correct and tells you nothing about income.
details.energy_note: Ninety-three per cent informal, and officially employed.

details.aspect: Women are worse on every sub-measure
details.description: Q2 2024: unemployment 5.1% female against 3.4% male; youth time-related underemployment 11.2% female against 7.1% male; self-employment 88.3% female against 82.2% male. Higher self-employment here means less formal work, not more entrepreneurship.
details.energy_note: Worse on unemployment, underemployment and informality, all three.

details.aspect: The graduate pipeline does not clear
details.description: Roughly 1.7 million graduates leave Nigerian universities and polytechnics annually without the economy absorbing them.
details.energy_note: One point seven million graduates a year, into what.

details.aspect: And the advocacy figures are not reliable either
details.description: A 2025 youth report claimed nearly 80 million Nigerian youth are unemployed, which is implausible against the NBS rate and appears to conflate unemployment with inactivity and informality. Both the official and the advocacy number mislead in opposite directions.
details.energy_note: One number too low, one far too high, neither usable.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the methodology change
details.description: Under the old methodology Nigerian unemployment rose from 14.2% in 2016 to 33.3% in 2020. Under the new ILO-aligned methodology, Q2 2024 unemployment was 4.3% with time-related underemployment at 9.2%, self-employment at 85.6% and informal employment at 93.0%. The two series are not comparable, and nothing on the ground changed between them.
details.energy_note: Thirty-three per cent, then four, and the same streets.

issues.title: Working informally, which is most people
issues.category_name: Work, unemployment and what a degree is worth
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
issues.summary: 93% of employment is informal, which means no contract, no pension, no sick pay, no maternity provision, and no mechanism when something goes wrong.

details.aspect: Nothing accrues
details.description: Thirty years of work in the informal sector produces no pension record, no employment history a lender recognises, and no entitlement at the end.
details.money_note: Value of unaccrued entitlements over a working life.
details.energy_note: Thirty years of work, and no record that it happened.

details.aspect: Maternity is unpaid absence
details.description: Without formal employment there is no maternity entitlement, so the weeks before and after a birth are weeks with no income, in the health context of MAT-001.
details.energy_note: Giving birth, and simply not earning for two months.

details.aspect: Illness stops the income the same day
details.description: No sick pay means the trading day missed is the income missed, which is why people work through conditions that then become the chronic ones in SOM-001.
details.energy_note: Working ill, because the stall does not pay itself.

details.aspect: And credit costs more without a record
details.description: No payslip means informal lending at punitive rates, which is where the ransom and medical borrowing in SEC-001 and HLT-001 actually comes from.
details.energy_note: Borrowing at the worst rate, for the worst reasons.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the day she could not open
details.description: Malaria on the Tuesday. The stall does not open Tuesday or Wednesday. That is NGN 18,000 of margin and the rent is on Friday, so she opens on Thursday still unwell and is worse for a fortnight.
details.energy_note: Two days closed, and a fortnight of being worse for it.

issues.title: The name on the CV, abroad
issues.category_name: Work, unemployment and what a degree is worth
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Before any question of qualifications, the name on the application changes the callback probability - which is one of the best-evidenced findings in labour economics.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the foundational experiment
details.description: Bertrand and Mullainathan sent nearly 5,000 fictitious resumes to help-wanted ads in Boston and Chicago, half with white-sounding names and half with African-American-sounding names. White names received 50% more callbacks. Applicants with white names needed about 10 resumes per callback; those with African-American names needed about 15.
details.energy_note: Fifty per cent more callbacks, for the name alone.

details.aspect: The finding that matters most
details.description: For white names a higher-quality resume produced 30% more callbacks. For African-American names it produced a far smaller increase. Improving the CV does not close the gap, which means the usual advice does not work.
details.energy_note: Getting better qualified helps them more than it helps you.

details.aspect: Equal-opportunity employers were no different
details.description: Federal contractors, larger employers and employers explicitly stating they are Equal Opportunity Employers did not treat the African-American resumes more favourably.
details.energy_note: The declaration on the advert made no measurable difference.

details.aspect: And it has not improved
details.description: A meta-analysis of field experiments found the trend since 1990 close to flat, sloping slightly upward - no change in the rate of discrimination against African Americans over three decades.
details.energy_note: Thirty years of measurement, and a flat line.

details.aspect: The honest caveats
details.description: Callbacks are not hires, so the effect cannot be converted directly into earnings. Darolia et al. argue many audits overstate discrimination by using very stereotypical names, and found no callback gap when pairing typically-white first names with typically-black surnames. Recorded because the counter-evidence belongs in the row.
details.energy_note: Strong finding, real methodological dispute, both stated.

details.aspect: Which is why people change the name
details.description: Shortening, anglicising, or using a middle name measurably improves callbacks and costs something that is not measured anywhere.
details.energy_note: Getting the interview by not being yourself.

issues.title: What a woman's work is assumed to be
issues.category_name: Work, unemployment and what a degree is worth
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
issues.summary: High female self-employment and informality are read as entrepreneurial culture. They are the residue of exclusion from formal work.

details.aspect: Self-employment as the leftover category
details.description: 88.3% of employed Nigerian women are self-employed. That figure is celebrated in some framings and describes, mostly, trading at subsistence margins because formal employment was not available.
details.energy_note: Called entrepreneurship. Mostly it is a stall.

details.aspect: Childcare does not exist as a purchasable service
details.description: Where extended family is dispersed and incomes are low, the childcare that would release a woman into formal work is neither affordable nor available.
details.energy_note: No nursery, no grandmother nearby, no job.

details.aspect: Capital is the binding constraint and is gendered
details.description: Collateral is usually land, land is usually inherited, and inheritance is WOM-004. The credit constraint on a woman's business traces directly to a customary law the Supreme Court already struck down.
details.energy_note: No land, therefore no collateral, therefore no loan.

details.aspect: And the outcome is attributed to ambition
details.description: Lower female earnings and smaller female businesses are read as preference or risk appetite rather than as the sum of the constraints above.
details.energy_note: Blamed for a result the inheritance law produced.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the loan officer
details.description: She wants NGN 3 million to expand the shop. The bank asks for collateral. The family land is in Nnewi and is in her brothers' names because of the custom Ukeje v Ukeje struck down in 2014. The loan officer is sympathetic and the answer is still no.
details.energy_note: Refused a loan by a custom the Supreme Court voided.

details.aspect: And the aggregate is read as a preference
details.description: Smaller female businesses, lower female earnings and higher female informality are then presented as evidence about women's ambition or risk appetite, rather than as the arithmetic sum of the collateral rule, the childcare absence and the commute.
details.energy_note: A statistic produced by land law, filed under ambition.

issues.title: A name the form cannot hold
issues.category_name: Names: spelling, screening and identity mismatch
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Nigerian names are long, tonal, frequently multi-part, and carry diacritics that systems strip. The result is a person whose documents do not agree with each other, through nobody's error.

details.aspect: Diacritics are dropped and tone is lost
details.description: Yoruba names carry tonal marks that most systems cannot store. Ọlámidé becomes Olamide, and the version on the passport becomes the only lawful spelling of a name that was never spelled that way.
details.energy_note: The official version of your name is the one the computer could manage.

details.aspect: Length limits truncate
details.description: Airline fields cap at around 30 characters. A full name of four parts is silently cut, and the truncated form then does not match the passport at check-in.
details.energy_note: Your name, shortened by a character limit, at the gate.

details.aspect: Which part is the surname is not obvious
details.description: Staff unfamiliar with the convention enter the wrong field, producing records where the given name and family name are swapped - across a bank, an employer and a university, differently each time.
details.energy_note: Filed under your first name in three databases.

details.aspect: And marriage changes it again
details.description: A name change on marriage must be propagated across every registry separately. Any registry not updated produces a mismatch that is treated as the woman's error rather than the system's.
details.energy_note: Married, and now inconsistent everywhere at once.

details.aspect: Downstream failures persist for years
details.description: Inconsistent names produce background-check mismatches, payroll failures, credit file fragmentation and benefit refusals long after any immigration question is settled.
details.energy_note: A transcription from 2011, still failing checks in 2026.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the certificate that is not hers
details.description: Her WAEC certificate reads ADEYEMI Folasade Aduke. Her degree reads Folashade Adeyemi. Her passport reads Folasade Aduke ADEYEMI. The credential evaluator returns all three as unverifiable pending a sworn affidavit of one and the same person, which costs money and six weeks.
details.energy_note: Three documents, one woman, six weeks.

issues.title: The identity is frozen before you reach the airport
issues.category_name: Names: spelling, screening and identity mismatch
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Air travel locks a vetted identity at booking. A mismatch found later cannot be fixed at the desk by anyone, for technical reasons rather than unhelpfulness.

details.aspect: How the lock works
details.description: A booking creates a Passenger Name Record, which generates passenger data sent to government screening before a boarding pass can issue. Once vetting completes the identity is frozen; changing a surname means changing the vetted identity, which requires re-vetting that cannot happen in real time.
details.energy_note: Not a rule a supervisor can waive. A sequence that cannot be rerun.

details.aspect: eVisas are bound to the exact passport MRZ
details.description: Many electronic authorisations are cryptographically linked to the machine-readable zone, so a single character's deviation invalidates the authorisation outright.
details.energy_note: An authorisation voided by one letter.

details.aspect: The defensive practice is expertise most travellers never need
details.description: Copy the spelling from the MRZ, use the same passport for every booking and profile, contact the airline before check-in rather than at the airport.
details.energy_note: Specialist knowledge, about your own name.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - thirty characters
details.description: OLUWASEUNFUNMI ADEBAYO-OGUNDIMU is 31 characters with the hyphen. The booking system stores 30. At check-in in Doha the name on the pass is one letter short of the passport and the supervisor explains, correctly, that nobody at the airport can re-run the security vetting.
details.energy_note: A flight lost to a field length.

issues.title: Sharing a name with somebody
issues.category_name: Names: spelling, screening and identity mismatch
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Name-based screening produces false positives, and clearing one is not a thing that can be done once.

details.aspect: Institutions act first and ask later
details.description: A name match triggers a hold, a review or a closure, because the cost of a wrong freeze falls on the customer and the cost of a missed match falls on the institution.
details.energy_note: Account frozen for a name you share with a stranger.

details.aspect: There is no central register to be cleared from
details.description: No certificate of innocence exists to present. Each institution repeats the process independently, indefinitely.
details.energy_note: Proving it again, at every new institution, forever.

details.aspect: Common names carry the most exposure
details.description: The most ordinary names in the population are the most likely to collide, so being unremarkable is itself the risk factor.
details.energy_note: Penalised for having a common name.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the shared name
details.description: There are a great many Chukwuemeka Okaforso. His transfer is held for review for nineteen days. The bank will not say why and is not permitted to. The landlord does not accept nineteen days as an explanation.
details.energy_note: Nineteen days, for a name thousands of people have.

issues.title: The officer who decided, and the one who would not have
issues.category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the officer who decided
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: A large share of the hurdles in this dataset are not policy. They are one person's decision on one day, which another person would have made differently, and which is then permanent.

details.aspect: Same file, different answer
details.description: The same documents, a different desk, a different outcome. Everyone who deals with these systems knows this, and nobody can demonstrate it in their own case.
details.energy_note: Refused by someone who was having a bad morning.

details.aspect: Discretion is unappealable because it is discretion
details.description: Where the decision-maker is entitled to weigh factors, there is no error of law. Being wrongly assessed is not a ground of appeal; being unlawfully assessed is, and from outside the two are indistinguishable.
details.energy_note: Not wrong enough to appeal, wrong enough to end it.

details.aspect: The informal payment is the shadow price of discretion
details.description: A decision that can go either way is a decision that can be sold. Every discretionary step in DOC-002, AIR-004 and POL-001 has a tariff for exactly this reason.
details.energy_note: Discretion, with a price list.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the two sisters
details.description: They apply on the same day, with the same sponsor, the same bank statements and the same itinerary, for the same wedding. One is issued and one is refused, and the refusal letter cites intent to return.
details.energy_note: Identical applications, opposite answers.

issues.title: The error that becomes your record
issues.category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the officer who decided
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: A wrong date, spelling or status code entered once is copied forward by every later system, and the burden of disproving it is entirely the person's.

details.aspect: Databases copy, they do not verify
details.description: The error propagates from the first record into every downstream system, each of which then treats the others as corroboration.
details.energy_note: One typo, confirmed by four systems.

details.aspect: You are presumed to be the unreliable party
details.description: The person asserting the record is wrong is the one whose account is doubted. Institutions trust their own data over the human being in front of them.
details.energy_note: Your word against a field.

details.aspect: Correction requires an original that may not exist
details.description: Fixing it means producing the authoritative source document from an archive that may be paper, may be in another state, and may have burned.
details.energy_note: Correct it by producing a document from a building that flooded.

details.aspect: And the age on the record governs everything
details.description: Where birth registration was informal, the recorded date of birth may be an estimate made by a clerk - which then determines school entry, exam eligibility, employment age limits and pension date for the rest of the life.
details.energy_note: A guessed birthday, governing sixty years of eligibility.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the birthday a clerk chose
details.description: Registered at four years old, the clerk wrote 1 January because the mother gave a season rather than a date. That 1 January governs her school entry, her exam eligibility, her employment age limit, her NYSC call-up and the year she may draw a pension. It is wrong by about eight months.
details.energy_note: Sixty years of eligibility, resting on a guess.

issues.title: The file nobody can find
issues.category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the officer who decided
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
issues.summary: Verification in Nigeria frequently depends on a physical record held by an institution with no functioning archive, and the absence is treated as the applicant's problem.

details.aspect: Paper, in a room, in another city
details.description: School results, land records, court files, service records. Retrieval means travelling there, finding the clerk, and paying the person who knows which cabinet.
details.energy_note: A day's travel, to a cabinet, and a tip to the man who knows it.

details.aspect: Verification tokens have their own market
details.description: Where results are confirmed by scratch card or online token, the token is scarce, resold and sometimes counterfeit - so verifying a genuine result can fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the result.
details.energy_note: A genuine certificate, unverifiable for want of a card.

details.aspect: The foreign institution reads absence as fraud
details.description: An unanswered verification request abroad is treated as a failed one, so an archive problem in Nigeria presents in London as a suspected forgery.
details.energy_note: A missing filing cabinet, read as a lie.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the 1998 result
details.description: The university needs confirmation of her WAEC sitting. The board's records for that centre for that year are incomplete. She has the original certificate in her hand. The admissions office requires confirmation from the board, and the board cannot confirm what it cannot find.
details.energy_note: Holding the certificate, and unable to prove it.

issues.title: Being read as dishonest before you speak
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: The brief asks for the psychological effects of being seen as bad. For Nigerians the content of the stereotype is specifically dishonesty, which means the suspicion attaches to the person's word rather than to their capability.

details.aspect: A stereotype about honesty is worse than one about competence
details.description: Incompetence can be disproved by performance. Dishonesty cannot be disproved at all - every success can be re-read as a better deception, which is why the usual advice to work harder does not resolve it.
details.energy_note: You cannot out-perform an accusation of lying.

details.aspect: The pre-emptive over-documentation
details.description: Volunteering references, receipts, certificates and screenshots before anyone asks. It is exhausting, it is rational, and it reads to the recipient as slightly odd - which is its own cost.
details.energy_note: Proving yourself before anyone has doubted you, and looking strange doing it.

details.aspect: Women carry a doubled version
details.description: Simultaneously assumed to be a potential fraud and a potential victim - suspected for the nationality and patronised for the gender, frequently by the same person in the same conversation.
details.energy_note: Suspected and pitied, at once, by the same colleague.

details.aspect: Anger at the actual fraudsters, with nowhere to go
details.description: Resentment among ordinary Nigerians toward the people who built the reputation is intense, and voicing it abroad reads as confirming the stereotype rather than distancing from it.
details.energy_note: Furious at them, and unable to say so without sounding like them.

details.aspect: Children inherit it without the context
details.description: A second-generation child is asked about the prince joke in a playground in a country their parents chose, with no framework for it and no memory of Nigeria at all.
details.energy_note: A nine-year-old in Croydon, explaining 419.

details.aspect: It suppresses the visibility that would eventually change it
details.description: Starting the company, taking the platform, publishing under your own name - the things that would replace the stereotype are exactly the things it makes expensive.
details.energy_note: The cure is the thing it prices out.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the email signature
details.description: He stops putting Lagos in his signature and starts writing 'GMT+1'. Response rates improve. He knows exactly what that means and has never mentioned the change to anyone.
details.energy_note: Removing the city from the signature, and it working.

issues.title: The relationship market, with the nationality priced in
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: The brief names this directly. The identity changes who will partner with you, on what terms, and how the relationship is read by everyone around it - and the romance-scam association gives it a specific and unusually corrosive content.

details.aspect: The scam association poisons the ordinary approach
details.description: Because the best-known Nigerian presence in online dating is fraudulent, a genuine Nigerian man making a genuine approach is met with a suspicion specific to his nationality. The irony recorded in REP-001 applies: the actual scammers are posing as white Americans.
details.energy_note: He is real, and the fake ones have made that the hard part.

details.aspect: Being used and discarded is a real pattern
details.description: Relationships in which the Nigerian partner is a novelty, a project, or a story rather than a person - warm, intense, and ended once the cost of association becomes concrete. The harm is that the interest was never in the person.
details.energy_note: Fascinating for a season, and then inconvenient.

details.aspect: Visa suspicion contaminates genuine relationships
details.description: A relationship between a Nigerian and a citizen of a wealthier country is assessed by friends, family and the state as a possible immigration route, so the couple must prove sincerity to people who did not ask to be involved.
details.money_note: Cost of evidencing a genuine relationship to an immigration authority.
details.energy_note: Proving you are in love, to a government, in writing.

details.aspect: At home the market is shaped by the economics
details.description: Marriage expectations attach to a man's earning capacity in an economy described in ECO-001, and to a woman's age and family standing - so both sides are assessed against criteria that the rest of this dataset makes harder to meet.
details.energy_note: Judged on a salary the currency keeps shrinking.

details.aspect: Widowhood and divorce reprice a woman entirely
details.description: The widow in WOM-005 and the divorced woman face a narrowed market, custody consequences and a social status that is assigned rather than chosen.
details.energy_note: Re-sorted, by an event she did not cause.

details.aspect: And isolation removes the thing that buffers everything else
details.description: Partnership is the largest single protective factor against every stressor in this dataset. A market distorted by stereotype, documents and economics removes it from the people carrying the most.
details.energy_note: The main shock absorber, priced out of reach.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the third date
details.description: It is going well. She asks, lightly, what he does, and he says he works in crypto compliance, which is true. There is a pause that is a quarter-second too long. He has learned to hear that pause and he hears it now.
details.energy_note: A true answer, and the quarter-second after it.

issues.title: Not being able to plan
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
issues.summary: Currency movement, power failure, insecurity and administrative unpredictability together remove the assumption of continuity that any long project requires.

details.aspect: Long-horizon commitments stop being rational
details.description: A degree, a business, a house, a pension. Each requires believing the conditions in five years will resemble today's, and the evidence does not support that belief.
details.energy_note: Never starting the thing that takes five years.

details.aspect: So the horizon shortens to the next quarter
details.description: Short-horizon, low-commitment activity is the correct adaptation, and it is also the activity with no compounding returns - which is the mechanism by which a rational individual choice produces a stagnant aggregate.
details.energy_note: Everyone behaving sensibly, and nothing compounding.

details.aspect: Emigration becomes the only plan anyone has
details.description: When domestic accumulation does not work, japa is not aspiration but arithmetic - and it becomes the organising topic of a national conversation, affecting people who never go.
details.energy_note: A country where the only plan is the exit.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the deferred wedding
details.description: They planned 2023 and a two-bedroom in Magodo. Then fuel, then the naira, then her father's hospital deposit. They are still engaged, aged 34 and 31, living in separate family houses, and they have stopped naming a date.
details.energy_note: Engaged indefinitely, by exchange rate.

issues.title: The arithmetic that never stops
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
issues.summary: Running a household under ECO-002 is continuous mental computation - prices, credit, who is owed, what can wait - and it occupies the same capacity that would otherwise go to work or study.

details.aspect: Scarcity consumes working memory
details.description: Continuous budgeting under genuine constraint measurably reduces the cognitive capacity available for anything else. The effect is a consequence of the condition, not a trait of the person in it.
details.energy_note: A calculator running in your head, all day, for years.

details.aspect: And the load is invisible to everyone else
details.description: The household appears to function. What it costs to make it function is not observable, which is why the person doing it is described as coping.
details.energy_note: Praised for coping, which is the description of the injury.

details.aspect: Decision fatigue produces the expensive mistakes
details.description: After enough small decisions the large ones are made badly, which is when the bad loan is taken and the wrong school fee is deferred.
details.energy_note: Worst judgement, exactly where it matters most.

details.aspect: It transmits to the children as a temperament
details.description: Children raised in continuous financial vigilance acquire it. The capable, anxious, over-responsible adult is a predictable output and is usually described as a personality.
details.energy_note: Competent at nine, exhausted at forty.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the market arithmetic
details.description: Tomatoes are up again. She recalculates the week in her head at the stall: swap the fish for eggs, defer the kerosene, the school levy is Thursday, her sister owes her NGN 4,000 and will not have it. She does this four or five times a day and has done for eleven years.
details.energy_note: Five recalculations a day, for eleven years.

issues.title: The one who left, and the one who stayed
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Japa splits families into senders and receivers, and the remittance relationship carries obligation, guilt and quiet resentment in both directions.

details.aspect: The obligation has no ceiling
details.description: Whatever is sent, more is needed, because prices move and the needs are medical. There is no amount that discharges it and no point at which the sender is finished.
details.money_note: Annual remittance load.
details.energy_note: A bill that is never paid in full.

details.aspect: It delays the sender's own life by a decade
details.description: Deposit, pension, training, children - deferred to fund a household on another continent. Measured at sixty, the remittance decade is not recoverable.
details.energy_note: Your thirties, spent on somebody else's survival.

details.aspect: And returning without visible success is not an option
details.description: A return with nothing to show is read as failure by an extended family that may have funded the departure, which is why people stay abroad in conditions they would not accept at home.
details.energy_note: Staying away, because coming back would have to be explained.

details.aspect: The one who stayed carries the actual work
details.description: Hospital visits, funerals, property, the ageing parent. Money is sent; presence is not, and the sibling who stayed knows precisely which of the two is harder.
details.energy_note: He sends money. She sits with their mother.

details.aspect: Neither can say any of this out loud
details.description: The sender cannot complain about the cost without sounding ungenerous; the receiver cannot complain about the absence without sounding ungrateful. Both learn to talk around it, permanently.
details.energy_note: A subject the whole family talks around.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the December question
details.description: Every December someone asks when he is coming home. He has not been in four years. The airfare is real but it is not the reason, and he cannot explain the actual reason without describing a life that sounds like failure.
details.energy_note: Four years, and an answer he cannot give.

issues.title: What it takes out of the work
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: The brief asks specifically about efficiency and growth. The costs are real, large, and attributed to the person rather than to the conditions in essentially every setting.

details.aspect: Infrastructure failure is a productivity tax before it is anything else
details.description: Power, connectivity, transport and water each fail unpredictably, and each failure is absorbed by rescheduling the work around it. The output loss is never attributed to the grid.
details.energy_note: Losing a morning to the generator, weekly.

details.aspect: Administrative load is a second unpaid job
details.description: Passports, visas, verifications, appeals, bank reviews, utility disputes. Days per year, every year, drawn from the same hours as the career.
details.time_note: Days per year on the administration of the hurdles in this file.
details.energy_note: A second job, unpaid, with no promotion in it.

details.aspect: Threat monitoring runs on the same budget as thinking
details.description: Sustained vigilance about security, money and status consumes the attention that would go to work. The capacity is finite and already committed.
details.energy_note: Concentration spent before the day begins.

details.aspect: Sleep goes first, and everything is downstream of sleep
details.description: Generators, heat, night-time power windows, the folder of pending applications. Degraded sleep degrades judgement, mood and output invisibly.
details.energy_note: Everything else, downstream of not sleeping.

details.aspect: The result is scored as a character trait
details.description: Reduced output is appraised by employers, universities and families as laziness or unreliability. The person receives that judgement and frequently agrees with it.
details.energy_note: Judged for capacity that was already spent.

details.aspect: Which closes the loop of this entire dataset
details.description: Conditions are imposed. The conditions reduce output. The reduced output is read as evidence about the person and about Nigerians. That evidence is then used to justify the conditions - the visa refusal, the extra verification, the blocked payment.
details.energy_note: Made unable, then blamed for it, then restricted because of it.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the morning
details.description: Power went at 04:00. The inverter is flat, so the generator runs from 07:00, so the fuel needs buying, so the queue, so the deliverable that was due at noon is sent at 16:40 with an apology. Her client in Berlin has no framework for any of this and records her as unreliable.
details.energy_note: A morning lost to fuel, filed abroad as unreliability.

details.aspect: The loop closes here
details.description: The conditions reduce the output. The reduced output is read as a fact about Nigerians. That reading justifies the visa refusal in VIS-001, the extra verification in REP-003 and the blocked payment in FIN-002 - each of which costs more time, and reduces the output further.
details.energy_note: Made unable, blamed for it, and restricted because of the blame.

issues.title: Back pain, and the fact that it is measured
issues.category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
issues.summary: The brief asks about back pain specifically. It is not a figure of speech: Nigeria may carry one of the heaviest low back pain burdens in the world, and the rural figure is roughly double the urban one.

details.aspect: The national burden, against comparators
details.description: Nigeria may have one of the greatest burdens of low back pain in the world, with a one-year prevalence of 40-85% against 14-51% reported elsewhere in Africa, and a point prevalence of 33-40% against 10-33% in high-income countries such as the UK, Canada and Belgium.
details.energy_note: Up to eighty-five per cent, in a year.

details.aspect: Rural against urban
details.description: One-year prevalence runs between 70% and 85% in rural Nigeria against 39% urban - roughly double, which points at manual labour, distance to care and the water-and-fuel carrying in PWR-001.
details.energy_note: Seven in ten, in the villages.

details.aspect: By occupational group
details.description: Farmers 74.4%, professional drivers 73.5%, industrial workers 59.7%, nurses in Ibadan 44.1%. Healthcare workers in Sokoto: lifetime 56.2%, annual 39.1%, point prevalence 17.2%, with older age, female sex, longer practice, overweight and lifting patients significantly associated.
details.energy_note: Three quarters of farmers, three quarters of drivers.

details.aspect: It is treated by continuing to work
details.description: With 93% informal employment and no sick pay, the response to back pain is to keep lifting - which converts an acute episode into the chronic condition that then cannot be treated at all.
details.energy_note: Working through it, until it is permanent.

details.aspect: And 'it is stress' is heard as 'it is not real'
details.description: Where a clinician identifies a psychosomatic component, the explanation lands as an accusation of fabrication. The pain is real and the mechanism is real; the wording does the damage.
details.energy_note: Told it is in your head, about a back that hurts.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the prevalence figures
details.description: Nigeria may carry one of the greatest burdens of low back pain in the world: a one-year prevalence of 40-85% against 14-51% elsewhere in Africa, and a point prevalence of 33-40% against 10-33% in the UK, Canada and Belgium. Rural one-year prevalence runs 70-85% against 39% urban. By occupation: farmers 74.4%, professional drivers 73.5%, industrial workers 59.7%, nurses in Ibadan 44.1%.
details.energy_note: Up to eighty-five per cent of rural adults, in a year.

issues.title: The stress of running a household, in the spine
issues.category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Nigerian nationality and being female
issues.summary: The single most directly relevant finding in this dataset to what the brief asked: Nigerian women who appraised their domestic responsibilities as very stressful had roughly three times the odds of low back pain.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the Ibadan domestic-work study
details.description: Among rural Nigerian women, two-month prevalence was 58% for low back pain, 30% for neck and shoulder pain and 30% for elbow, hand and wrist pain. Women who appraised their domestic responsibilities as very stressful had significantly higher odds: OR 2.88 for low back pain, 4.58 for neck and shoulder pain, 1.88 for elbow, hand and wrist pain.
details.energy_note: Nearly three times the odds, for finding the housework stressful.

details.aspect: High demand and low control, specifically
details.description: The same study found high-demand/low-control conditions associated with higher low back pain odds at OR 2.58. That is the exact structure of unpaid domestic labour: the demands are fixed by others and the control is nil.
details.energy_note: Lots of demands, no authority, and it lands in the back.

details.aspect: The psychosocial factors outweighed the biomechanical ones
details.description: A population-based study in Nigeria found psychosocial factors the most important correlates of both self-reported and performance-based disability, while aggregate biomechanical exposure was not - though the authors flag a possible healthy-worker effect, since the rural population studied were all heavy manual workers.
details.energy_note: It is not only the lifting. It is the conditions around the lifting.

details.aspect: Which is the mechanism the brief was pointing at
details.description: PSY-004 describes the arithmetic that never stops. SOM-002 is the measured output of it. The load is not metaphorical and the link is in the peer-reviewed literature rather than asserted here.
details.energy_note: The stress, and the spine, in the same regression.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the woman who is fine
details.description: Water from the borehole twice daily, forty litres. Firewood. Three children under seven. Her husband's mother, who is bedbound. She is thirty-four and has had back pain for four years and has never mentioned it to anyone, because everybody she knows has it.
details.energy_note: Four years of pain, unremarkable because it is universal.

issues.title: Depression, arriving as a physical complaint
issues.category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Nigeria, any gender
issues.summary: Psychological distress in Nigeria commonly presents somatically, which means it is investigated as a physical problem, not found, and the patient is left believing nobody could identify what is wrong.

details.aspect: The comorbidity in musculoskeletal patients
details.description: Among older Nigerian adults with musculoskeletal disorders, severe depressive symptom prevalence was 61.3%, with predictors including age 70 or over (OR 2.23) and female gender (OR 3.45).
details.energy_note: Six in ten, and women at three and a half times the odds.

details.aspect: And in adolescents
details.description: A south-eastern Nigerian study of adolescents found 54% reported symptoms involving the body and 62.5% had either head or body features - described in the literature as a neglected issue.
details.energy_note: Half of them, presenting with the body.

details.aspect: The honest counterpoint
details.description: Gureje et al. found Nigerians had lower somatization prevalence than Latin American comparators. The picture is not uniform and this row records the disagreement rather than choosing the more dramatic figure.
details.energy_note: Not settled. Recorded as unsettled.

details.aspect: The investigative loop is expensive
details.description: Presenting with chest pain, then abdominal pain, then headache produces successive negative workups, each with a fee, in a pay-at-point-of-use system.
details.energy_note: Four investigations, all negative, all paid for in cash.

details.aspect: And psychiatric care is scarcer than the rest of it
details.description: The workforce gap in HLT-001 is most acute in mental health, so the correct referral frequently has nowhere to refer to.
details.energy_note: Correctly diagnosed, and no one to send you to.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - depression among musculoskeletal patients
details.description: Among older Nigerian adults with musculoskeletal disorders, severe depressive symptom prevalence was 61.3%, with predictors including age 70 or over (OR 2.23) and female gender (OR 3.45). In adolescents in the south-east, 54% reported symptoms involving the body and 62.5% had either head or body features.
details.energy_note: Six in ten, and women at three and a half times the odds.

issues.title: The productivity loss nobody has quantified
issues.category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Nigerian nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: The brief asks about effects on efficiency and growth. The honest position is that the components are well evidenced and the total is not, because the study joining them has not been done.

details.aspect: HONEST GAP - the combined study does not exist
details.description: Searches of this literature surface low back pain prevalence, occupational musculoskeletal burden, somatisation and depression separately. No study was located combining somatic symptom scales with back pain and psychological distress in a Nigerian worker sample, and none quantifying absenteeism or output loss. This row says so rather than inventing a figure.
details.energy_note: The mechanism is documented. The number is not.

details.aspect: What can be said from the components
details.description: One-year low back pain prevalence of 40-85%, 61.3% severe depressive symptoms among older adults with musculoskeletal disorders, OR 2.88 linking domestic stress to back pain, and 20-200 days a year of administrative load from PSY-006. Each has a known effect on output; nobody has multiplied them together for this population.
details.money_note: Order of magnitude only. Do not cite.
details.energy_note: Four large effects, never added up.

details.aspect: Why the study is not done is itself part of the dataset
details.description: Research requires funding, institutional stability, and researchers who have not emigrated. EDU-001 and HLT-002 each remove one of those.
details.energy_note: The evidence gap has the same causes as the harm.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the study that did not happen
details.description: The researcher who would have run the combined worker-cohort study - somatic scales, back pain and psychological distress in one sample - finished her doctorate in 2021 and has been in Leeds since 2022. Her department has not replaced her. The gap recorded in this issue and the reason for the gap are the same person.
details.energy_note: The missing study and the missing researcher are one absence.
